hits.full_text:
In many cases, you'll find the only thing preventing you from learning is your ego.

No one enjoys feeling foolish, but attempting something new requires that you climb down from your perch and struggle as a beginner. You must ask questions that reveal your ignorance or attempt skills that make you look uncoordinated. 

Learning demands the willingness to live in a brief state of discomfort. You must believe that looking like a fool for an hour will not ruin your reputation for life.
hits.hook: James Clear: ego is what stops most learning; you have to be willing to look foolish as a beginner (~57k views, 510 saves)
hits.draft_en: Starting something new at any age means being bad at it in front of people for a while. I'm trying to treat that as part of the price, not as proof that I'm too late.

reply_ideas.description: a mathematician announcing the Journal of Handwritten Mathematics, where every paper must be written with a fountain pen and sent by snail mail
reply_ideas.reply_text: I'd subscribe just to see the crossed-out lines in the proofs. Do the referee reports have to come back by mail too, and does an ink blot on a key step count against you?

reply_ideas.description: an ADHD planner arc that ends with the planner in a drawer by day 5, and the idea of skipping the empty box and writing today's date on the next line
reply_ideas.reply_text: The drawer of half-used planners is such a common story. I wonder if all the stickers on day one set a bar that no ordinary Tuesday can reach. Have you ever tried opening a new planner to the middle on purpose, so there's no perfect first week to break?

reply_ideas.description: a post about being stressed over a reading journal that hasn't been updated since summer, described as homework they assigned themselves that no one else cares about
reply_ideas.reply_text: Homework you assigned yourself is somehow the hardest kind to turn in late. Could you write one line for each book since summer and call yourself caught up? I'm curious which one you'd most want to remember.

x_posts.title: The planner drawer
x_posts.text:
Is there a drawer in your house with a few planners in it, each one used for about a week?

I've started to think the planner didn't fail. The first week was set up to be perfect, and no regular Tuesday can live up to that.

x_posts.title: Crossed-out lines
x_posts.text:
A mathematician just announced a journal where every paper has to be written with a fountain pen and sent by mail. I honestly can't tell if it's a joke, and more than 600 people liked it anyway.

I think a lot of us miss work that still shows where we crossed things out.
